Five classes implement `Notifier` (defined in `src/notifiers/notifier.ts:8` as `notify(event: TaskEvent): void`), all declaring it explicitly:

| Class | Location |
|---|---|
| `EmailNotifier` | `src/notifiers/emailNotifier.ts:3` |

| `SmsNotifier` | `src/notifiers/smsNotifier.ts:3` |

| `ConsoleNotifier` | `src/notifiers/consoleNotifier.ts:3` |

All five are registered in the `notifiers` array at `src/index.ts:12`.

Two notes on completeness: TypeScript interfaces are structural, so a type can satisfy `Notifier` without the `implements` clause — I grepped every other source file for a `notify` member and found only one such case, `src/scheduler/dispatcher.test.ts:9`, which is an object literal test fake rather than a class. And `src/scheduler/dispatcher.ts:6` consumes `Notifier[]` but doesn't implement it.
